description.from:
Outcome: Owner decision D (Ryan, 2026-11-08): because launching a site cannot require code or deploy steps, every shared-tier tenant signs in through ONE Cognito user pool with ONE Google identity provider (one Google OAuth client owned by us) and ONE app client. The callback set stays tiny and fixed: https://newsroom.p.apyr.us/ (and its /newsroom forms), the CLI loopback callbacks, and localhost for development; it never grows with tenants, so Cognito's 100-callback-URL limit per app client never binds. A person signs in first and picks the site after (tenant switcher, PPY-0bb0fd); a tenant's own host sends /newsroom to the shared host with the site preselected (state parameter carries only the site id, checked against TenantDomain). Scoping after sign-in is by membership: the pre-token Lambda issues role claims only for a TenantMembership the person holds. Google sign-in only; never create Cognito password users (the shared pool disables self-service username/password sign-up; email:true in defineAuth is reviewed for the shared stack).

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): amplify/auth/resource.ts (defineSiteAuth on the shared stack: fixed redirect URLs, Google only), amplify/auth/redirect-urls.ts, amplify/functions/tenant-claims, app/newsroom sign-in and switcher, middleware.ts, docs/google-oauth-setup.md.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features/shared-sign-in.feature):
Scenario: A new site needs no sign-in configuration change
    Given tenant "harbour-news" was just provisioned
    When its admin opens harbour-news.p.apyr.us/newsroom
    Then she signs in with Google on newsroom.p.apyr.us and lands in harbour-news, and the app client's callback list did not change

Scenario: Signing in grants nothing without membership
    Given Bo signs in with Google and holds no membership
    Then he sees no site and every tenant model returns nothing

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-0bb0fd, PPY-130eb2. Blocks PPY-496c0b. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: Browser tests with two tenants; synth test that the shared callback list is fixed.
Rollout: With the shared stack (M4).
Risk and mitigation: Risk: one Google client's consent screen names Papyrus, not the tenant. Mitigation: accepted for v1; bring-your-own client later (PPY-496c0b).

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: changes: sign-in configuration of the shared stack.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).

Prospectus side (kanbus-3e5e82): one shared Google OAuth client and one Cognito client for every shared-tier deployment; Prospectus authorize takes the deployment, checks that the token is bound to it (host or audience), that the Account owns the deployment and that the person is a member, and returns capabilities combined with billing standing. Papyrus's pre-token Lambda issues role claims only for the deployment authorize approved, and TenantMembership roles are granted only to Account members. Ryan's rules: ONE shared Google client by default; later a tenant may bring its own (PPY-496c0b, kanbus-3c5b8b); Google sign-in only, never Cognito password users.
